title.zh: 秦汉：统一多民族国家的建立和巩固

clips.send: Sea travel also grew under Emperor Wu: fleets sailed from Xuwen (Guangdong) and Hepu (Guangxi), through Southeast Asia, to southern India — the beginning of the “Maritime Silk Road”.

clips.send: In 60 BCE the Western Han set up the Protectorate of the Western Regions. From then on, the region of today’s Xinjiang came under the central government and became an inseparable part of China.
clips.text: In 60 BCE the Western Han set up the Protectorate of the Western Regions. From then on, the region of today’s Xinjiang came under the central government and became an inseparable part of China.

clips.send: After Zhang Qian, an overland route took shape: from Chang’an through the Hexi Corridor and today’s Xinjiang to West Asia, and on to Europe. So much Chinese silk travelled west along it that it is called the “Silk Road”.

clips.send: In the late Warring States period Qin grew strong. From 230 to 221 BCE King Ying Zheng conquered Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi, founding the Qin dynasty — China’s first unified, multi-ethnic, centralized state — with its capital at Xianyang.

clips.send: Qin’s harsh rule provoked revolt. In 209 BCE Chen Sheng and Wu Guang rose up at Dazexiang — the first large-scale peasant uprising in Chinese history. Qin fell in 207 BCE; after the Chu–Han war, Liu Bang founded the Western Han in 202 BCE with its capital at Chang’an.

clips.send: Memory hook: Order of Qin’s conquests: Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan, Qi. Silk Road: Chang’an (today: Xi’an), Hexi Corridor, Xinjiang, West Asia, Europe.

clips.send: The First Emperor ran the regions through commanderies and counties — 36 commanderies at first, later more than 40. Meng Tian drove back the Xiongnu and a wall was built from Lintao in the west to Liaodong in the east; in the south the Lingqu Canal joined the Xiang and Li rivers.

clips.send: Under Emperor Wu (r. 141–87 BCE) the Western Han reached its height. His generals Wei Qing and Huo Qubing drove back the Xiongnu and took the Hetao region and the Hexi Corridor, where four commanderies were set up: Wuwei, Zhangye, Jiuquan and Dunhuang.

clips.send: To win the Yuezhi as allies against the Xiongnu, Emperor Wu sent Zhang Qian to the Western Regions in 138 BCE; he went again in 119 BCE. His journeys strengthened ties between the Central Plains and the Western Regions.

clips.send: In 25 CE Liu Xiu founded the Eastern Han with its capital at Luoyang. Ban Chao restored Han control of the Western Regions and sent Gan Ying toward Daqin; Gan Ying reached the Persian Gulf. Cai Lun improved papermaking. Under Qin and Han the unified multi-ethnic state was built and consolidated.

clips.send: 战国后期，秦国日益强大。从前230年到前221年，秦王嬴政先后灭掉韩、赵、魏、楚、燕、齐六国，建立起中国历史上第一个统一的多民族的中央集权国家——秦朝，定都咸阳。

clips.send: 汉武帝时，海上交通也发展起来：船队从今广东徐闻、广西合浦等地出发，经过东南亚，到达印度半岛南部。这是“海上丝绸之路”的开端。

clips.send: 烽火台（烽燧）。传递军情的信号站。沿着长城每隔一段距离就修筑一座烽火台。发现敌情时，白天放烟、夜间举火，一座接一座传递下去，军情很快就能传到后方。长城不是孤立的一道墙，而是由城墙、关隘、烽火台等组成的防御体系。

clips.send: 25年，刘秀建立东汉，定都洛阳。东汉时，班超经营西域，还派甘英出使大秦，一直到达波斯湾；宦官蔡伦改进了造纸术。秦汉时期，统一多民族国家得以建立和巩固。

clips.send: 张骞通西域后，一条从长安出发，经河西走廊和今新疆地区，运往西亚，再转运到欧洲的陆上通道逐渐形成。大量中国丝和丝织品经此西运，这条路被称为“丝绸之路”。

clips.send: 汉武帝时（前141—前87年在位）西汉达到鼎盛。他派卫青、霍去病北击匈奴，夺取了河套和河西走廊地区，并在河西走廊设置了武威、张掖、酒泉、敦煌四郡。

clips.send: 秦始皇在地方推行郡县制，把全国分为三十六郡（后来增加到四十多郡）；派蒙恬北击匈奴，修筑西起临洮、东至辽东的万里长城；在南方开凿灵渠，沟通湘江和漓江。

clips.send: 前60年，西汉设置西域都护，管辖西域。从此，今新疆地区开始隶属于中央政权，成为我国不可分割的一部分。

clips.send: 六国货币。统一前：形状、大小、轻重各不相同。战国时期各国货币不统一：齐、燕等国用刀币，韩、赵、魏等国多用布币，秦国用圆形的圜钱，楚国用蚁鼻钱。货币不统一，不便于各地的经济交流，也不便于国家征收赋税。

clips.send: 竹简与小篆。统一文字。战国时各国文字写法不一，同一个字往往有好几种写法。秦统一后，以小篆作为标准字体在全国推行；后来又推行更便于书写的隶书。统一文字促进了文化交流，对中华文明的传承意义重大。

clips.send: 秦的暴政激起反抗。前209年，陈胜、吴广在大泽乡起义，这是中国历史上第一次大规模农民起义。前207年秦朝灭亡；经过楚汉之争，前202年刘邦建立西汉，定都长安。

clips.send: 长城（秦）。抵御匈奴的军事防御工程。秦始皇派大将蒙恬北击匈奴，收复河套地区。为防御匈奴，秦朝把原来秦、赵、燕三国北部的长城连接起来并加以修筑，形成西起临洮、东至辽东的万里长城。长城是中华民族的象征，是世界建筑史上的奇迹。

clips.send: 为了联络大月氏共同夹击匈奴，汉武帝于前138年派张骞出使西域；前119年张骞再次出使西域。张骞通西域，加强了中原和西域的联系。
